company_items.summary: Citigroup posted strong Q3 EPS of $2.85, up 27% and beating the Street's $2.65 estimate, on slightly better revenue of $23.85B versus $23.72B expected. The efficiency ratio improved 290 basis points to 59%, provisions came in slightly below estimates, and investment banking fees rose 9% year-over-year with equity underwriting surging 77%. Full-year guidance was nudged higher on both net interest income — now expected up mid-to-high 6% versus prior 5-6% — and ROTCE, now guided to 11% versus the prior 10-11% range.

sectors: Large-cap bank earnings showing strength in FICC, equities trading, and investment banking fee generation, with improving efficiency ratios and reserve-build discipline.
tts_summary: Here is your earnings update for the morning of October 13th. This is a focused earnings recap centered on one name — Citigroup — and it is a clean beat across the board. Citigroup delivered third-quarter earnings per share of two dollars and eighty-five cents, up 27% year-over-year and well ahead of the Street's estimate of two sixty-five. Revenue came in at twenty-three point eight five billion, edging past the consensus of twenty-three point seven two billion. The beat was not just a top-line story — expense discipline was a meaningful contributor, with the efficiency ratio improving 290 basis points to 59%, versus the Street's expectation of 60.7%. Provisions were also slightly lighter than feared at two point five eight billion versus two point six five billion estimated, and they did build reserves of three hundred sixty-nine million during the quarter, so this is not a case of releasing reserves to juice the number. Within the investment bank, fixed income currencies and commodities revenue rose 4% to four point three eight billion, beating the four point two six billion estimate. Equities revenue climbed 14% to one point seven two billion, a touch light of the one point seven seven billion consensus. Investment banking fees were a standout, up 9% to one point three five billion versus one point two six billion expected, with equity underwriting absolutely surging — up 77% year-over-year. On guidance, management nudged the full-year outlook higher in two key areas. Net interest income guidance was raised, with the company now expecting revenue growth in the mid-to-high 6% range versus the prior 5 to 6% range. Return on tangible common equity was also tightened higher to 11%, up from the prior range of 10 to 11%. The bottom line here is that Citigroup delivered on efficiency, held the line on credit quality, grew fee revenue meaningfully, and raised the bar for the rest of the year. This is a bullish print that should keep the tone constructive around large-cap bank earnings this season.
